chunks: Sa'd, from Musa ibn al-Hasan, from Abu al-Qasim 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Hammad al-Kufi, from Bashir, from Abu Maryam al-Ansari, who said:

I was with Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام in a garden belonging to him. Then the time for salat came, so he drew a bucket for wudu (ablution) from a well of his, and there came up on it a piece of dry excrement. So he tipped it away with his head and performed wudu (ablution) with the remainder.
Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: We have already explained the basis of this report earlier.

key_terms.الْبَاقِيِ: the remaining water after the impurity was cast off
key_terms.الْخَبَرِ: the report or hadith under discussion
key_terms.الْوُضُوءِ: wudu (ablution), the ritual washing before prayer
key_terms.رَكِيٍّ: a well from which water was drawn
key_terms.عَذِرَةٍ: excrement, mentioned here as an impurity

ai.seo_question: Can wudu (ablution) be performed with well water if a dry impurity is found in the bucket?
ai.summary: This hadith relates an incident in which Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام used water drawn from his well for wudu (ablution) after a dry piece of excrement appeared on it and was cast aside. In context, the report is used in discussions of ritual purity and the legal rulings concerning water and contamination.
